question.text: Which of the following best describes 'materiality' in an impact-assurance engagement under SAS-100?

answer.text: Only monetary misstatements exceeding 5% of revenue
Material only means front-page newspaper mentions
Any matter, whether monetary or non-monetary, that could reasonably influence a stakeholder's assessment of the SE's social impact

explanation.text: The Logic: Materiality in impact-assurance is broader than financial materiality. It covers any quantitative OR qualitative misstatement that could influence a stakeholder's assessment of impact — e.g., omitting a programme closure, overstating a geographic footprint, or mis-classifying outcomes as impact. The Trap: A and C apply financial-audit thresholds inappropriately. D is trivialisation. Cross-Exam Context: Impact materiality is broader than SA 320 financial-audit materiality — mirrors GRI Standards and SASB. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Agree a two-tier materiality framework with the SE at engagement planning: (i) quantitative — e.g., 5% of total beneficiaries; (ii) qualitative — any undisclosed programme closure, regulatory notice, or safeguarding incident. Document both in the engagement letter.
